study.title: Daniel 12 - Hope, sealing and perseverance to the end
study.overview: Daniel 12 concludes the vision with three great emphases: God intervenes in behalf of his people in the time of distress, there is a resurrection and final judgment, and the servant of God must follow faithfully to the end without requiring control over dates and details. The chapter combines comfort and mystery: it consoles because history is not abandoned to the power of the wicked; it preserves the mystery because the full meaning of these words is only clarified in fulfillment. The final promise to Daniel is not satisfied curiosity, but of rest, resurrection and inheritance.

outline.title: Delivering in the time of anguish and the resurrection
outline.explanation: Michael stands up for the people of God just when affliction reaches the peak. The people inscribed in the book are delivered, and the text goes from historical suffering to eschatological hope: many rise, some for eternal life and others for shame and contempt. The wise shine, showing that faithfulness and instruction in righteousness have permanent value before God.

outline.title: The sealed book and the search for understanding
outline.explanation: Daniel must keep and seal the words until the time of the end, indicating that not everything would be immediately understood. The vision was not given to satisfy curiosity, but to be preserved until the divinely appointed moment. The scene of the two beings by the river enters the question about the outcome of the announced wonders.

outline.title: The determined period and the purification of the people
outline.explanation: The messenger swears that events will take place after a limited time, until the power of the holy people is broken. Daniel still does not understand, and receives again the order to move forward, because the content is sealed until the time of the end. Suffering will have a purifying effect: many will be refined, the wicked will persist in wickedness, and only the wise will understand.

outline.title: The prophetic calendar and final promise to Daniel
outline.explanation: Two milestones of days linked to the withdrawal of the continual sacrifice and the devastating abomination are mentioned, and then a bliss for those who persevere until the end of the period. The chapter closes with a personal word to Daniel: he must proceed to the end, rest and then resurrect to receive his inheritance at the end of the days.

study.context: The chapter fits at the end of the great vision begun in the previous chapters, after the prediction of intense afflictions about the people of God. The notes received relate this section to both the tribulations suffered by the Jewish people and, by extension, to the afflictions of the church in later times, without requiring a unique identification for all the details. The text emphasizes that the complete knowledge of the outcome belongs to God and will be fully understood only in fulfillment.
study.theology: Daniel 12 affirms God's sovereignty over history, the reality of a heavenly protection in favor of his people and the hope of the final resurrection. The inscription in the book indicates belonging to the Lord and points to a divine criterion of salvation and preservation. The chapter also teaches that the suffering of the saints is not useless: it can serve to purify, refine and distinguish between the wicked and the wise. In evangelical Christians, this points to the confidence that God leads history to final judgment and restoration, and that present fidelity is lived in the light of eternal life. bliss are not in overmining the secrets of the calendar, but in persevering to the end under the promise of rest, resurrection, and inheritance.

scholarViews.insight: The time of anguish culminates in the resurrection of the dead; the former ransoms of God in Daniel foreshadowed this final deliverance.
The prophecies of affliction are accompanied by comfort taken from Christ and the future life, to sustain God's people in difficult times.
Daniel 12 is understood as the conclusion of the great prophesied revolutions, culminating in the general resurrection and the rest of Daniel in his inheritance.

questions: How will the promise that the wise will shine confronts our search for immediate recognition in this world?
How can suffering, without being good in itself, serve to purify and mature the people of God?
What changes in the way we live when we remember that Daniel was called to walk to the end, and not to control God's calendar?
study.practice: Long live this chapter with two united attitudes: perseverance and trust. Perseverance, because the order for Daniel is to keep walking to the end, without paralyzing before what he does not understand. Trust, because the end is not defeat for those who belong to the Lord, but rest, resurrection and inheritance. In practice, this means maintaining daily fidelity, resisting evil even when it seems to prosper, and sustain the Christian hope that God will end history with justice.
study.uncertainty: The biblical text here is highly symbolic at various points, and the notes provided do not allow to safely identify all historical referents of the periods of days or certainly detail the relationship between each image and specific events. Nor is it possible to affirm, based only on the notes given, a single interpretation closed for the expression about the continual sacrifice and the devastating abomination. The readings presented by the commentators should be read as interpretations, not as equivalent to the undeniable final sense of the chapter.
